title: Khichdi on a Pole
blurb: A freezing night, a stolen prize, and a pot that will not cook.
script:
[warmly] In the cold part of the year, when the river outside Delhi ran like ice… Emperor Akbar made an announcement.

[grandly] “A thousand gold coins,” he said, “to anyone who can stand in that river all night. From dusk… until the sun comes up. [short pause] No fire. No blanket. Just you… and the cold water.”

[curious] Many people came to look at the river. [amused] Most of them put one toe in… and went straight home again.

[gently] But one poor man had a family to feed. And he thought about his children… and he walked into the water… and he stood there.

[softly] All night. In the dark. While the stars moved slowly over Delhi.

[cheerfully] And in the morning, shivering and blue and grinning, he came to the palace for his thousand gold coins.

[surprised] But one of the ministers stood up. [slyly] “Your Majesty,” he said, “I have a question. Was there anything else nearby? Any light? Any warmth?”

[calmly] “There was a lamp,” said the poor man. “Far away, on the palace wall. I could see it across the water.”

[firmly] “AH!” said the minister. “Then he was WARMED by the lamp! He did not stand in the cold alone! [grandly] The prize must not be given.”

[worried] And the court murmured, and nodded, and agreed with the loudest man in the room, the way courts sometimes do.

[sadly] The poor man walked home with nothing.

[thoughtful] Now, Birbal was not in court that day. [gently] But when he heard about it, he did not argue. He did not shout. [amused] He simply did not come to work.

[curious] One day passed. Two days. On the third day, Emperor Akbar sent for him. “Birbal! Where have you BEEN?”

[calmly] “Cooking, Your Majesty,” said Birbal. “I am making khichdi. You are welcome to come and see.”

[curious] So the Emperor came. And in Birbal's courtyard he found a fire… a small one… burning on the ground.

[surprised] And high, high above it… tied to the top of a tall bamboo pole… swinging gently in the air… was a pot.

[incredulous] “Birbal,” said Akbar slowly, “that pot is nowhere NEAR the fire.”

[cheerfully] “Not near, Your Majesty. But the fire is in the same courtyard. [slyly] It will cook. I am told these things carry.”

[short pause] And Emperor Akbar went very quiet.

[softly] Because he understood. [gently] If a lamp across a whole river could warm a man… then a fire across a courtyard could surely cook a pot of rice.

[warmly] “Take the pot down,” said the Emperor. “And send for that poor man. [firmly] He has earned every coin.”

[amused] And Birbal took the pot down, and put it on the fire where it belonged, and the khichdi was very good. [long pause] [whispers] Though the Emperor, they say… never quite finished his bowl.
